A shape-memory alloy can recover a trained form when heating drives a transformation from low-temperature martensite toward high-temperature austenite. Below the transformation range, martensite is relatively easy to deform; heating above the finish temperature allows the austenitic structure to restore the trained geometry. An exception arises if strain exceeds the recoverable limit or causes permanent damage: heating then cannot fully restore the original form. Transformation temperatures and recoverable strain depend on alloy composition and processing, so one specification cannot be assumed for every shape-memory alloy.

{"source":"A shape-memory alloy can recover a trained form when heating drives a transformation from low-temperature martensite toward high-temperature austenite. Below the transformation range, martensite is relatively easy to deform; heating above the finish temperature allows the austenitic structure to restore the trained geometry. An exception arises if strain exceeds the recoverable limit or causes permanent damage: heating then cannot fully restore the original form. Transformation temperatures and recoverable strain depend on alloy composition and processing, so one specification cannot be assumed for every shape-memory alloy.","flashcards":[{"question":"How does heating produce shape recovery in a shape-memory alloy?","answer":"Heating through the transformation range converts deformed martensite toward austenite, which restores the trained geometry above the finish temperature."},{"question":"When may heating fail to restore a shape-memory alloy fully?","answer":"Recovery may be incomplete when strain exceeds the recoverable limit or causes permanent damage; the limits depend on composition and processing."}]}
